name: Turnip Works
summary: A free 3D tabletop in a browser tab where buildings furnish themselves; players join from a link. We make it, so read this row with that in mind.

dims.note: a 3D table you turn and tilt; a top-down view too

platform.note: desktop or laptop browser with WebGL 3D graphics, tested most in Chrome

accounts.note: the GM starts a table and sends links; whoever opens a link takes that seat

fog.note: per player: each sees what their pawn's light and line of sight reach; the GM sees all

lighting.note: lamps and fires light the rooms; walls, darkvision and lamps decide each player's sight

mapbuild.note: drop a building (tavern, crypt, tower...) and its rooms furnish themselves; rooms drawn by hand; hills and caves are on dev (not yet live)

levels.note: buildings with several floors and stairs, a cut-height view to see inside; hills and rooms below ground on dev (not yet live)

sheets.note: no character sheets or rules engine; pawns keep a damage count, conditions, notes and a link to your own sheet; initiative and turn order

ddb.note: Beyond20 rolls, hit points and conditions land on pawns: built, on dev (not yet live)

dice.note: 3D physics dice rolled on the table, seen by everyone

phone.note: live: may open, not built for touch or small screens; a phone pass (tap to place, two fingers to turn) is on dev (not yet live)

offline.note: no offline mode or self-hosting guide; the code is public, so running your own is possible in principle

opensource.note: engine AGPL-3.0, every 3D asset CC BY 4.0

ai.note: an outside AI chat assistant can sit at the table as the GM's helper through a web API; the 3D art was generated with AI, then picked and fixed by hand; most code is written by AI coding agents

modding.note: a plain web API (made for AI helpers) can read the table and send commands; no add-on or module system

stage.note: new (public since October 2026) and changing every week; things can break

community.note: brand new: a handful of alpha tables, no public reviews yet

upsides: Drop a building on the table and it furnishes itself in seconds
Free, no account, no install: players join from a link
Open source (AGPL-3.0), and every 3D asset is CC BY 4.0
downsides: Alpha: new, changes weekly, and things can break
Needs a desktop browser with working 3D graphics; weak on phones (live)
No character sheets, rules engine, music or sound yet
